articles.headline: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns not expecting contract extension soon
articles.description: Karl-Anthony Towns says the chances "don't look good" for him getting a new extension with the Knicks before the start of the regular season.
articles.headlineJa: ニックスのカール＝アンソニー・タウンズ、早期の契約延長は見込んでいない
articles.descriptionJa: カール＝アンソニー・タウンズは、レギュラーシーズン開幕前にニックスとの新たな契約延長を得られる可能性は「低そうだ」と語った。
articles.body:
The New York Knicks take the court for their first preseason game Monday night, but one of the key players in last season's championship run remains at odds with the team over a contract extension.

"It don't look good," Karl-Anthony Towns said Monday of getting a new contract in place before the start of the regular season.

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million. He is due $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for next season.

Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that the Knicks' latest offer to Towns was a four-year deal worth approximately $200 million.

A six-time All-Star, Towns was a catalyst for the Knicks' playoff run last season, averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists as New York won the title in a five-game Finals over the San Antonio Spurs.

Does that mean the Knicks should reward Towns for his hand in ending a 53-year title drought?

"No s---, Sherlock," Towns said. "I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys [reporters] think I have something else to prove."

Knicks owner James Dolan has said the team will not go into the second spending apron, which means tough decisions will need to be made. New York did not re-sign backup center Mitchell Robinson this offseason. Robinson, who was the longest-tenured Knick on last year's team, signed with the Boston Celtics.

Towns said that he's aware of the challenges of maintaining a championship core but that in his estimation the team has not done enough to compromise.

"Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said. "None of those things have come close to happening."

Information from ESPN's Vincent Goodwill was used in this report.

articles.headline: Ben Johnson: Tyson Bagent will start at QB for Bears vs. Packers
articles.description: Tyson Bagent will be the Bears' starting quarterback for Sunday's game at the Packers, coach Ben Johnson announced Monday.
articles.headlineJa: ベン・ジョンソン：タイソン・バジェントがベアーズ対パッカーズ戦でQBとして先発
articles.descriptionJa: ベン・ジョンソンコーチは月曜日、日曜日のパッカーズ戦において、タイソン・バジェントがベアーズの先発クォーターバックを務めると発表した。
articles.body:
Tyson Bagent will be the Chicago Bears' starting quarterback for Sunday's game at the Green Bay Packers, coach Ben Johnson announced Monday.

"Tyson will be the guy," Johnson said in his weekly appearance on ESPN 1000 in Chicago.

It will essentially be Bagent's second straight start in place of the injured Caleb Williams, however Case Keenum was credited with the start in Week 4 against the New York Jets.

On the first play of Sunday's 23-12 victory, both Bagent and Keenum trotted onto the field. Keenum lined up in the shotgun and pitched the ball to running back D'Andre Swift for a 2-yard gain while Bagent was flanked out wide.

"Well, I got all these memos saying that Tyson was starting before I ever made an announcement, so I wanted to get Case out there," Johnson said after the game. "It was like his ceremonial first pitch out there. Handing off the torch."

With Bagent under center, the Bears dominated the Jets in time of possession (42:45 to 17:15) and generated more first downs (34) than the Jets had plays (32), the second game in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) when that's occurred. The Bears ran 89 plays, resulting in a plus-57 play differential that was the fourth largest by any team since the 1970 merger (the Browns' first game returning to the NFL in 1999 was the most recent).

Bagent went 25-of-34 for 268 yards and an interception in his first regular-season start in 1,059 days.

Williams has a Grade 2 hamstring injury that doctors say has a recovery time of three to four weeks, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Sept. 27. Sunday's game at Green Bay would be Williams' third game missed with his injury.

ESPN's Courtney Cronin contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Broncos get good news on Pat Surtain II's ankle, sources say
articles.description: Broncos star cornerback Pat Surtain II avoided a worst-case scenario on his ankle injury, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.headlineJa: ブロンコス、パット・サーテイン2世の足首の負傷に朗報
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスのスターコーナーバック、パット・サーテイン2世の足首の負傷について、最悪の事態は免れたことがNFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポート記者への情報源により明らかになった。
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos received some good news on both star cornerback Pat Surtain II and wide receiver Pat Bryant as MRIs taken showed both avoided worst-case scenarios, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Surtain suffered a non-contact ankle injury that saw him go to the ground as he grabbed his right foot and ankle until the Broncos' medical staff arrived. He was helped to the locker room by Broncos personnel and didn't return for the second half.

The 2024 Defensive Player of the Year, Surtain is the key to the Broncos' defensive gameplan each week, but sources say he's expected to only be out in the short-term.

Bryant is expected to miss "a few weeks," a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter. Bryant sprained his ankle in Sunday's loss and left the field on a cart.

Bryant is second on the Broncos this season with 122 receiving yards, while his nine receptions are tied with Courtland Sutton for second on the team. He has has a touchdown catch.

The Broncos next face the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday afternoon.

Information from ESPN's Jeff Legwold was used in this report.

articles.headline: Sources: Packers LB Edgerrin Cooper has torn Achilles
articles.description: Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper suffered a season-ending Achilles tear during Sunday's 17-14 victory over the Buccaneers, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：パッカーズのLBエジャリン・クーパーがアキレス腱を断裂
articles.descriptionJa: ESPNのアダム・シェフターとNFLネットワークのイアン・ラポポートによると、パッカーズのラインバッカー、エジャリン・クーパーが日曜日のバッカニアーズ戦（17-14で勝利）の最中にアキレス腱を断裂し、今季絶望となった。
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper suffered a season-ending Achilles tear during Sunday's 17-14 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Cooper underwent an MRI, which confirmed the nature of his injury.

The third-year pro went down without contact and reached for his lower left leg well away from where safety Xavier McKinney sacked Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels with 8:31 left in the third quarter.

Green Bay led 17-7 in the third quarter when it looked like Cooper was going to blitz on third-and-8 from the Bucs' 37 on Tampa Bay's first possession of the second half. On the play, he looked behind him as if someone kicked him in the back of the leg, but there was no one there. Cooper then pounded his fists into the turf before the medical staff reached him. He could not put any weight on his left leg and was ruled out shortly after he was carted off the field.

Cooper, a second-round pick in 2024, came into the game with 21 tackles, a team-best six tackles for loss and was second on the team with two sacks through the first three games. In 2½ quarters Sunday, he added nine more tackles, including a sack.

In the second quarter, Cooper's first interception of the season and second of his career helped give the Packers the lead. He picked off a Daniels pass with 36 seconds left in the first half that led to a 58-yard field goal by Trey Smack that put the Packers ahead 10-7 at halftime.

The Packers (2-2) held on to win despite two fourth-quarter turnovers thanks in part to the defensive performance without Cooper. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon blitzed on the Bucs' final three plays, and the result was a sack by safety Evan Williams, a short completion and a near interception by cornerback Keisean Nixon.

articles.descriptionJa: エリック・カラベルが、ファンタジーバスケットボールのドラフトにおいて、現在の平均指名順位では避けるべき選手を紹介する。
articles.body:
Give future Hall of Famer Kawhi Leonard credit for an outstanding 2025-26 season, as he averaged a career-best 27.9 PPG for the LA Clippers at age 34, and then emerged largely unscathed from offseason controversy to earn a new, generous two-year contract with one of his former teams, the Toronto Raptors. The Raptors feel like contenders again, and there is positive history as Leonard led them to an NBA championship in 2019.

Leonard not only carried the Clippers last season, but he finished among the top 10 fantasy options for roto/categories formats on the ESPN Player Rater, and just outside the top 10 in points leagues. Leonard incredibly managed to participate in 65 of the team's 82 games, and he delivered considerably better statistics than the year prior, when he looked just about done as a top fantasy option. He wasn't. Leonard played great.

Still, this is a player who turned 35 years old this summer, and with a long history of missing myriad games. The Raptors are built around terrific, young SF/SG Scottie Barnes, with Immanuel Quickley and RJ Barrett leading an underrated, deep backcourt, and hopefully anchor C Jakob Poeltl plays more minutes and more games than last season. The Raptors are making the playoffs in the challenging Eastern Conference whether Leonard plays in 60 games or not for the third time in the past seven seasons.

Investing in older NBA players with a history of missing games is dangerous in fantasy, regardless of format. Everyone else may have Philadelphia 76ers SF/PF LeBron James leading the avoid list, but James isn't going in the top 25 of most drafts. Leonard is. Thanks to the presence of Barnes, Leonard's usage in Toronto will precipitously decline. He will shoot less, and he will see fewer minutes. Fantasy picks in the first three rounds should come with some durability and performance assurances. Leonard is too much risk for me.

Welcome to the latest annual "Do Not Draft" list, repeatedly populated with brittle players that many fantasy managers dream about with little acknowledgement of risk. Hey, it's the truth!

Some of these names you will recognize from prior editions. The proper intention of this list is to analyze players with higher ADP marks than this analyst prefers, perhaps for various reasons. This is about value. There is far less risk of Kawhi Leonard in Round 5. In Round 2, no way.

Anyway, here are other players whose ADP doesn't seem to match actual value:

LaMelo Ball, PG, Minnesota Timberwolves: He led this list a season ago because he hadn't managed to play in 50 games in any of his past three seasons. Then Ball performed in 72 games last year. Problem solved! Well, not really. The Hornets heavily managed his minutes and his usage. Ball averaged barely 20 PPG. He was more efficient, but he still can't shoot well from the field. Superstar Anthony Edwards runs the Timberwolves show. Ball is an odd fit, and Round 3 is too early for him.

articles.headline: JJ Gabriel representatives demanded game time at Manchester United - sources
articles.description: Representatives of JJ Gabriel demanded that the teenager played at least 20 minutes in games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth before beginning talks about signing a scholarship with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: JJ・ガブリエルの代理人がマンチェスター・ユナイテッドでの出場時間を要求 - 関係者談
articles.descriptionJa: JJ・ガブリエルの代理人が、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドとの奨学金契約に関する交渉を開始する前に、サバFK、ブライトン、ボーンマス戦で少なくとも20分間の出場を要求したと、関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
Representatives of JJ Gabriel demanded that the teenager played at least 20 minutes in games against Sabah FK, Brighton and Bournemouth before beginning talks about signing a scholarship with Manchester United, sources have told ESPN.

Gabriel, 15, has not trained with United since walking out on the club ahead of their Carabao Cup tie with Brighton on Sept. 16.

He is pictured in United's squad photo, which was released on Monday. However, the image was taken nearly a month ago and sources have told ESPN there is little sign of a reconciliation with the club.

Gabriel's representatives believe certain promises made by Man United have also been broken, sources told ESPN.

Gabriel's representatives have been approached by ESPN for comment.

Gabriel, who turns 16 on Tuesday, was due to make his first team debut against Brighton before representatives demanded United cancel his registration over a row about his playing time.

He made his first-team debut in a preseason friendly against Atlético Madrid in the summer, but was omitted from the squad for the Champions League.

Sources have told ESPN that representatives told United he must play at least 20 minutes against Sabah, Brighton and in the Premier League fixture against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Oct. 25 before entering discussions over a scholarship.

Gabriel could have signed a pre-agreement from his 16th birthday on Oct. 6.

With it looking increasingly likely that Gabriel will leave, United, according to sources, are prepared to take legal action if there is evidence of other clubs approaching Gabriel outside of the rules.

They have yet to receive a formal enquiry.

A number of clubs have been linked with a move including Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Despite a breakdown in relations with Gabriel's camp, sources have told ESPN that they continue to believe Old Trafford is the best place for him to develop.

Club officials have made a number of attempts to check on his well-being since he stopped reporting for training.

- Barcelona sporting director: No interest in Man United's JJ Gabriel

- Rooney: 'Disappointing' if 'top player' JJ Gabriel leaves Man United

- Why Man United's wantaway wonderkid, JJ Gabriel, is so highly rated

Sources insist they have made every effort to show he has a pathway to the first team, including assigning coaches and specialist staff -- who usually only work with senior players -- to ensure he's prepared for the demands of professional football.

United also accepted a demand from Gabriel to be given the No.77 squad number for this season and petitioned the Premier League on his behalf to allow him to have the name "Gabriel JR" on his shirt.

Sources close to United insist they have prioritised Gabriel's well-being throughout his time at Old Trafford.

There has been a feeling internally that his representatives -- including members of his family -- have been more keen for the forward to break records rather than focus on his long-term development.

articles.headline: State of each position in 2026: What are the biggest tactical trends?
articles.description: Elite soccer has changed dramatically in recent years, and the most valued player skill sets have evolved as a result.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年の各ポジションの現状：最大の戦術的トレンドとは？
articles.descriptionJa: エリートサッカーは近年劇的な変化を遂げており、その結果、最も価値の高い選手のスキルセットも進化している。
articles.body:
Elite European soccer in 2026 feels decidedly different from what we've become used to. Over the past couple of seasons, the Premier League has been increasingly characterized by direct attacking, set pieces and long throw-ins. Many encounters between big clubs across Europe have become frenetic, end-to-end affairs, such as the Bayern Munich-Paris Saint-Germain semifinals in last season's UEFA Champions League.

A lot of the changes seem related to how teams play without the ball. The soccer we became accustomed to throughout the 2010s involved top sides trying to push their opponents back while keeping the ball. Once the ball reached the attacking third, they tried to outnumber defenders in key spaces and make use of their attacking talent.

One way for defensive sides to counter this approach is to use zonal marking, which involves defending space rather than individual players. They would set up in compact blocks and deny space in critical areas, whether they defended deep like Max Allegri's Juventus in the 2010s or pressed high like teams coached by Ralf Rangnick's disciples. While this tactic helps protect the areas closer to goal and prevent mismatches, it sometimes plays into the hands of those high-possession sides.

As a result, player marking (or man-to-man marking), in which defenders are assigned to follow attackers around up and down the pitch, started to make a comeback at the turn of the 2020s. Teams like Mikel Arteta's Arsenal and Andoni Iraola's Bournemouth combined this concept with their zonal marking, switching out of a zonal structure in certain situations to swarm teams attempting to move the ball forward (hybrid pressing). This makes moving the ball slowly up the pitch harder, causing teams to embrace more direct approaches with the ball.

Meanwhile, the game appears to be becoming more physical and more intense. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, every passing season of the Premier League has seen faster sprinting and more "high-intensity actions." And with off-ball physical data like running distance or top speed becoming more accessible, scouting departments now possess more transparent measures of athleticism, leading to players' athletic qualities being valued more.

Rather than just affecting the head coach's team talk, these big-picture changes have a major effect on the skill sets that clubs look for when assembling their starting XIs. Let's take a look at five positions -- goalkeepers, center backs, fullbacks, central midfielders, and strikers -- to see what has changed and why.

Goalkeepers: Distribution and cross-claiming

New Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has generated much buzz this season. One of his standout features has been his passing ability, playing quick passes to his center backs during the early buildup and exquisite floated long passes to Villa's forwards to escape pressure.

articles.body:
Bayern Munich are bracing for tough contract talks with star winger Michael Olise, while Chelsea lead the race for AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Bayern Munich are concerned about talks to renew Michael Olise's contract, as the winger hasn't yet told them if he even wants to stay in Bavaria, as reported by Sport Bild. The Bundesliga club is preparing for a very difficult negotiation with the representatives of the 24-year-old. One of the sticking points is that the France international wants a release clause in his new contract, something both Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala have. Bayern are willing to offer a mega contract that will run until 2032 but want an answer by next summer.

- Chelsea are leading the race to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who is also attracting strong interest from Liverpool and Arsenal, as reported by The Telegraph. Elsewhere, TEAMtalk have suggested that Real Madrid are considering becoming involved in the race for the 23-year-old after watching him closely in recent weeks. Los Blancos have watched Scott at least three times, including his first England start in the Three Lions' 7-0 victory over Croatia.

- Italian outlet Corriere dello Sport has offered an insight into the names Roma are looking at as they aim to sign a winger. In the summer, they looked at Stuttgart's Jamie Leweling and Chelsea's Jamie Gittens, who have both had a lack of game time since the summer transfer window shut so could be available for less than was demanded before. They also want Real Madrid's Endrick, hoping for a Donyell Malen-style deal where they have a loan with the option to make it permanent, and they aren't alarmed by AC Milan's interest. Frosinone's Giorgi Kvernadze is another player of interest.

- Juventus see Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Højbjerg as the leader Luciano Spalletti needs, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. They have previously looked at Leon Goretzka and Franck Kessié, who ended up at Aston Villa and Atalanta respectively, but remain keen on signing an older head for their midfield so are turning to the man who is captain for both Marseille and Denmark. There have already been exploratory contacts made about the 31-year-old, while Teun Koopmeiners is the main candidate to leave so he can come in.

- Juventus have recently made a move for Frosinone goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani and Inter Milan are monitoring him, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. Inter chief executive Beppe Marotta has insisted on a mix of foreign and Italian players, emphasizing the importance of a strong Italy squad. I Nerazzurri could decide to loan out the 22-year-old if they sign him, and they are also looking at Alessandro Romano, who is on loan at Cagliari from Roma.

articles.headline: Behind the scenes inside LeBron's first 76ers training camp
articles.description: From on-court schemes to a private team dinner to an attempt at divine intervention, here's what happened in LeBron's first camp with the 76ers.
articles.headlineJa: レブロン、76ersでの初トレーニングキャンプの舞台裏
articles.descriptionJa: コート上の戦術からチームのプライベートディナー、さらには神への祈りに至るまで、レブロンが76ersで過ごした初のキャンプで何が起きたのかを詳報する。
articles.body:
There might not be a more intriguing new-look team in the NBA this season than the Philadelphia 76ers.

It's not just the infusion of talent, but the rarity of the circumstances to acquire it that makes the Sixers so fascinating.

In any other year, signing forward Dean Wade to a four-year, $39 million contract and guard Anfernee Simons to a two-year, $12.3 million deal could be seen as a successful summer for a team coming off a second-round playoff appearance.

But then to trade for five-time All-Star Jaylen Brown two years after he led the Boston Celtics to the championship, making him just one of seven players in league history to change teams within two years of being named Finals MVP, made it an extraordinary offseason.

And adding LeBron James on a veteran's minimum contract made it potentially transformational.

With the Sixers playing their first preseason game Monday against the defending-champion New York Knicks, here are five key moments that have shaped their first week in training camp.

Monday, Sept. 28: four on the floor ... and a fifth in the group chat

Hours before media day opened with players posing for portraits and answering questions from local media members, the Sixers' four stars gathered on the practice floor.

They changed into their full uniforms later to be ready for photos. Their first order of business was a workout, not only to talk about, but demonstrate, how they can help one another.

All four had varying experience playing together, with Brown recently joining James and Tyrese Maxey for a few of their customary summer workouts in Los Angeles, and James playing with Joel Embiid on Team USA in 2024. But these first actions on the floor were tangible examples of the sacrifices this group has said it is willing to make for this season to be a success.

"Worked on getting to know each other," one team source told ESPN. "Camaraderie, rhythm, cadence and playing with each other."

With 36 All-Star appearances among them, each player has a game that commands extra attention from opposing defenses.

Philadelphia intends to exploit that by having its foursome work on two-man plays for when defenses inevitably overcommit.

"All four of those guys are going to be trapped somehow during the game, whether it's in the post or on the wing," the source continued. "We worked a lot on passing out of the post, making the extra pass to the corner."

Second-year guard VJ Edgecombe, the fifth starter on the team, was not part of these exercises, but there have been early indicators that he'll be included, too.

Edgecombe took it upon himself to start a group chat this summer for James and his new Sixers teammates.

"Before 'Bron got [here], I was like, 'Yo, I'm making a group chat: Me, 'Rese, JB, Joel,'" Edgecombe said of his initial plan he shared with Maxey. articles.headline: How a mass Man City player exodus would warp the transfer market
articles.description: If Manchester City are punished by being relegated from the Premier League, group of players worth more than £1 billion in transfer fees would suddenly become available.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ選手の大量流出が移籍市場をどう激変させるか
articles.descriptionJa: もしマンチェスター・シティが罰則としてプレミアリーグから降格することになれば、総額10億ポンド以上の価値がある選手たちが突如として移籍市場に放出されることになる。
articles.body:
What would happen to the transfer market if a group of players worth over £1 billion suddenly became available in the same window, all anxious to immediately find a new club?

If Manchester City fail to overturn an independent commission finding that they were guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-season period -- City reject the findings and lodged their appeal on Oct. 2 -- the soccer world will find out exactly what it looks like when a collection of superstars and serial winners flood the market.

It would be a football version of "Supermarket Sweep" with Europe's biggest clubs raiding the Etihad Stadium for cut-price deals. With few exceptions, players would be ready to take the first opportunity to escape the crumbling empire they were once so desperate join.

But it would also distort the market more than any previous situation. Chelsea super-charged the transfer market when Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich funded their high spending in the mid-2000s. City took it to another level following Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan's takeover in 2008 -- that spending is the root of the problems they now find themselves in with the Premier League. But if the exit doors are forced open at the Etihad, it will drive transfer fees down and change the whole landscape of the market.

With Premier League CEO Richard Masters saying last week that City "systematically broke Premier League rules for nearly a decade," the likelihood is high of tough sanctions on the club if their appeal fails. Potential punishments include expulsion from the league -- City could be kicked out and forced to apply to rejoin at the bottom of the English football pyramid -- or a huge points deduction that would make relegation to the second-tier Championship unavoidable.

That outcome -- dropping down just one division -- might prove to be the best-case scenario for City. But don't be fooled into believing that the club would be able to ride it out, keep their squad intact and seal an instant return to the top division.

The financial implications of dropping out of the Premier League, and the Champions League, would be seismic even for a club of City's stature and the inevitable outcome would be a mass exodus of their high-earning players.

Championship clubs receive just £5.7 million a year from the EFL's broadcast deal. Last season, City banked £248.9 million in prize money (£165.5 million from the Premier League, £83.4 million from the Champions League), so a hole of more than £240 million would immediately appear in their finances.

City's most recently published wage bill, for the 2024-25 season, amounted to £408.4 million. It is now likely to be closer to an annual £450 million following the arrivals of players including Gianluigi Donnarumma, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernández.

articles.headline: Ledley King backs Tottenham form to 'turn around very quickly'
articles.description: Ledley King has urged Roberto De Zerbi's team to draw on the experiences of last season to end the club's winless start to the new Premier League campaign.
articles.headlineJa: レドリー・キング、トッテナムの調子は「すぐに好転する」と支持
articles.descriptionJa: レドリー・キングは、ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ率いるチームに対し、昨シーズンの経験を活かして、プレミアリーグ新シーズンでの勝ちなしスタートから脱却するよう促した。
articles.body:
Former Tottenham captain Ledley King has urged Roberto De Zerbi's team to draw on the experiences of last season to end the club's winless start to the new Premier League campaign.

Spurs have been bottom of the table since a 3-2 loss at home to Aston Villa on Sept. 19, which made it two points from five league matches.

After a summer of lavish spending following successive 17th-placed finishes, expectations were raised, but League Cup winner King believes one positive result can act as a catalyst for Tottenham to turn around their form.

The situation was far more bleak for Spurs in March when De Zerbi arrived in north London with the singular focus to avoid a catastrophic relegation to the Championship.

Even though confidence was at an all-time low, De Zerbi masterminded survival after a 15-match winless run in the division was snapped and King believes that experience can help before Saturday's trip to Manchester United.

"It's been tough at the moment, but you can see signs of improvement game by game," King said at a recent Hall of Fame event at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"[They have] no choice. You have to find a way. Most of the group have gone through difficult periods and they managed to find a way out last season.

"They'll have to draw on that to a certain degree, but there is no easy way. You keep working on the training pitch, keep putting the work in.

"It's just a confidence thing. These are top players. I'm sure once the first positive result goes for the team, things can turn around very quickly. Just keep working hard, keep believing in yourself. That's the only way to do it."

- Andrew Robertson after hitting 100 Scotland caps: Hopefully I can catch Kenny Dalglish

- Roberto De Zerbi receives backing of Tottenham's chief executive

- Jan Paul van Hecke returns to Tottenham after suffering foot injury with Netherlands

Former England centre back King spent his entire career at Tottenham and made 323 appearances despite a long-standing knee injury.

King etched his name into club folklore with League Cup success in 2008 and as captain during Spurs' first venture into the Champions League two years later.

After the 45-year-old was one of four people inducted into the relaunched Hall of Fame last month, he received a thunderous reception as a half-time guest for the Villa match.

King said: "To be in the Hall of Fame is really humbling."

articles.headline: Folarin Balogun reopens door to Premier League despite failed Everton move
articles.description: United States striker Folarin Balogun has said that he would still be keen to play in the Premier League, even though his transfer deadline day move to Everton collapsed in dramatic fashion.
articles.headlineJa: フォラリン・バログン、エバートンへの移籍失敗後もプレミアリーグ復帰に意欲
articles.descriptionJa: アメリカ代表ストライカーのフォラリン・バログンは、移籍期限最終日にエバートンへの移籍が劇的な形で崩れたものの、依然としてプレミアリーグでのプレーに意欲的であると語った。
articles.body:
United States striker Folarin Balogun has said that he would still be keen to play in the Premier League, even though his transfer deadline day move to Everton collapsed in dramatic fashion.

Balogun, 25, backed out of a move to the Toffees after Everton and Monaco started to restructure the terms of his transfer after issues were raised during the his medical examination at Everton's Finch Farm training ground.

Asked by talkSPORT if a Premier League move is something that he'd still be interested in, Balogun said: "Yes, potentially.

"Football has many twists and turns as we've seen after the World Cup.

"I was close to a transfer, didn't materialise, but for sure it's definitely an option."

Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro said at the time that Balogun abandoned the move due to concerns over his treatment by the Merseyside club.

The former Arsenal forward continues to play his football at Monaco, after a high-profile summer in which he put in some solid performances for the USMNT at the World Cup but also found himself the subject of a major controversy.

Balogun picked up a red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the round of 32 and was subsequently banned from the USMNT's round of 16 clash with Belgium.

But then, the red card and ban were overturned by FIFA after U.S. President Donald Trump asked FIFA chief Gianni Infantino to review the decision.

Infantino said the decision was not influenced by Trump. Balogun was handed a suspended ban that allowed him to play against Belgium, but the UMSNT lost and were eliminated from the tournament.

- Folarin Balogun red card U-turn 'most serious incident in the history of football' - LaLiga boss

- Pochettino shares 'regret' over Balogun controversy, impact on USMNT

- David Moyes vents over Everton transfer window after Folarin Balogun deal collapse

Monaco are flying high in Ligue 1 and currently sit at the top of the table after five games, five points ahead of reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain.

Balogun's first match back for Monaco after the summer's transfer debacle was against Lens. Monaco won 2-1.

articles.headline: Premier League injury concerns from the international break
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 代表ウィークによるプレミアリーグの負傷者への懸念
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初の代表ウィーク中に発生した、プレミアリーグのスター選手たちの負傷に関する最新ニュースとアップデート。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.
